eligibility_note: Own panel FE estimation, 109 countries 2001-2014, internet/broadband/mobile on Gini (family 4), plus World Bank income-group splits.

results.correction: Middle income = World Bank upper-middle only.

heterogeneity.quote: Among middle- and high-income countries, increases in Broadband has a positive effect on income inequality, but the effect is barely detectable among low-income
Among the least developed economies, the marginal effect of Broadband is somewhat negative.
Higher levels of Urban dampens the marginal effect of Broadband in both models.

income_group_note: Table 6a/6b values match; low and lower-middle pooled (41 countries); 41+31+37=109.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: one-year lags only, no instrument or dynamic panel.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: per-100 use/subscription proxies, mobile max 215.5.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: unbalanced 830 obs, SWIID-driven coverage, short span.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: mean of 100 SWIID imputations, uncertainty ignored.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: quadratic GDP, many interactions, collinearity admitted and quadratic dropped in splits.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: only some interactions reported; plausible but not verified against footnotes.
risk_of_bias.why: Standard FE panel with Driscoll-Kraay SEs, but 'effect'/'impact' language and lags only for simultaneity; serious is defensible (borderline moderate).

problems: Minor: results horizon labelled contemporaneous but regressors are lagged one year. Intro says 107 countries, elsewhere 109 (noted by extractor, confirmed). No invented content found.
